informal.MainTheoremOfPolytopes: The Minkowski–Weyl theorem — a set is a V-polytope iff it is a bounded H-polytope.
informal.Vpolytope_of_Hpolytope: Every bounded H-polytope (finite intersection of half-spaces) is the convex hull of a finite point set.

records.title: Minimum modulus for the unique multiset-sum problem
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact minimum modulus `N_min(n) = 2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}` for the unique multiset-sum problem on the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}`, and proves the sharp elementary-abelian-2-group lower bound `k >= n - 1` for unique multiset sums in `(Z/2Z)^k`.

informal.MinModulus.nmin_eq: Proves that among moduli `N >= 2` the least one making the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}` valid for the unique multiset-sum problem is `2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}`, for every `n >= 2` (stated as `IsLeast`).
informal.MinModulus.elementaryAbelianTwoGroups_op: Proves that if `g_0, ..., g_{n-1}` in `(Z/2Z)^k` have unique multiset sums, then `k >= n - 1`: an elementary abelian 2-group admitting such a family has order at least `2^(n - 1)`.

records.title: Misere combinatorial games
records.abstract: Formalizes a combinatorial game theory library for misere play, including comparison modulo universes, p-free forms, outcome-stability, Property X, and concrete rulesets such as Hackenbush.

informal.MisereGames.Form.Promain.of_universe: Shows that comparison modulo a universe is characterized by the maintenance-proviso test.
informal.MisereGames.IntegerInvertible.isPFree_of: Proves that Property X makes the sum of two short p-free games p-free in an outcome-stable, hereditary, integer-invertible monoid.
informal.MisereGames.Form.Preservation.endLikeSee: Proves that universal closure gives a bijection from bounded end-like seeds to universes.

records.title: Monlib4 Operator-Algebra and Quantum-Set Core
records.abstract: Formalizes monlib4's finite matrix-algebra inner-automorphism theorem, unitary inner automorphisms, star-preserving linear maps, the structural core of quantum sets, the core Schur-product definition of quantum graphs, and a self-contained digit-sum divisibility theorem.

informal.Matrix.automorphism_matrix_inner: Shows that any automorphism of a finite nontrivial matrix algebra is implemented by an invertible intertwining matrix.
informal.Matrix.aut_mat_inner: Packages matrix-algebra automorphisms as inner automorphisms induced by a linear equivalence of the underlying coordinate space.
informal.Matrix.aut_mat_inner': Packages matrix-algebra automorphisms as conjugation by an element of `GL n 𝕜`.
informal.Matrix.aut_mat_inner_trace_preserving: Proves that automorphisms of finite matrix algebras preserve trace.
informal.Matrix.innerAut: Defines the linear map induced by conjugation with a unitary matrix.
informal.Matrix.innerAut_apply_trace_eq: Proves that unitary inner automorphisms preserve matrix trace.
informal.Matrix.innerAut.spectrum_eq: Proves that unitary inner automorphisms preserve the spectrum of the associated linear operator.
informal.LinearMap.IsReal: Defines star-preserving, or real, function-like maps.
informal.LinearMap.real: Defines the star-conjugate involution on linear maps.
informal.QuantumSet: Defines the monlib4 quantum-set structure with modular automorphisms and a fixed orthonormal basis.
informal.Complex.quantumSet: Instantiates the complex numbers as the base quantum set.
informal.schurMul: Defines the Schur product of linear maps using multiplication, tensoring, and coalgebra comultiplication.
informal.QuantumGraph: Defines quantum graphs as Schur-idempotent endomorphisms.
informal.QuantumGraph.Real: Defines real quantum graphs as Schur-idempotent, star-preserving endomorphisms.
informal.nat_repr_mod_eq_sum_repr_mod: Proves that the value represented by digits in base `a + 1` has the same remainder modulo `a` as the sum of those digits.
informal.nat_dvd_repr_iff_nat_dvd_sum_repr: Proves the generalized digit-sum divisibility criterion for base `a + 1` modulo `a`.

records.title: Monsky's Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Monsky's theorem that a square can be dissected into n triangles of equal area if and only if n is nonzero and even, via a 2-adic valuation, a three-coloring of the unit square, and a rainbow-triangle argument.

informal.LeanPool.Monsky.monsky_theorem: Proves that the unit square admits a dissection into n equal-area triangles if and only if n is nonzero and even.

records.title: Geometric Four-Colorings of the Moser Lattice and Ring
records.abstract: Formalizes the two explicit parity colorings from Dúcz's 2026 note on the Moser lattice. The development derives the exact quadratic norm formula, proves that the integer-coordinate embedding is faithful, proves both colorings proper and geometric on the entire lattice, and descends them through localization by powers of three to the Moser ring. As a structural corollary, every unit-distance graph realized entirely in the Moser ring is four-colorable. The uniqueness classification of geometric four-colorings and the chromatic number of the full Euclidean plane are not claimed.

informal.LeanPool.MoserLatticeColorings.MoserRing: The two parity maps defined by Dúcz descend to proper four-colorings of the full Moser ring, and equality of colors for each map depends only on Euclidean distance.
Every abstract graph with a realization in the Moser ring that sends each edge to a unit-distance pair is four-colorable.

records.title: MRiscX
records.abstract: A Hoare logic for verifying unstructured RISC-V-like assembly in Lean, following Lundberg et al. (SEFM 2020), with a certified interpreter, proved structural Hoare rules, per-instruction specifications, custom elaborators and tactics, and a complete One-Time-Pad correctness proof.

informal.hoareTripleUp: Defines the MRiscX Hoare triple, asserting that from any state satisfying the precondition the code reaches a successor state satisfying the postcondition while respecting the line whitelist and blacklist.
informal.S_SEQ: Proves the sequencing Hoare rule, peeling off the last instruction of a code block.
informal.PRE_STR: Proves the precondition-strengthening rule for MRiscX Hoare triples.
informal.POST_WEAK: Proves the postcondition-weakening rule for MRiscX Hoare triples.
informal.specification_LoadImmediate: Proves the per-instruction Hoare specification of the load-immediate instruction.
informal.proof_otp: Proves the full correctness of a One-Time-Pad implementation written in MRiscX assembly.

records.title: Neukirch's Algebraic Number Theory: Hilbert ramification theory
records.abstract: Formalizes Hilbert's ramification theory for Galois extensions of number fields, including the fundamental identity and the decomposition and inertia groups, ported from the jjdishere/neukirch project.

informal.NumberField.ramificationIdx_mul_inertiaD: Proves the fundamental identity g·e·f = [L : K] for a Galois extension of number fields.
informal.NumberField.finrank_eq_ramificationIdx_m: Shows that when P is the unique prime over p, the degree [L : K] equals the ramification index times the inertia degree.
informal.NumberField.IsMaximal_conjugates: Proves the Galois group acts transitively on the primes lying over a fixed prime.
informal.NumberField.DecompositionGroup_card_eq_r: Computes the order of the decomposition group as the product of the ramification index and inertia degree.
informal.NumberField.InertiaFieldAutEquivResidueF: Identifies the Galois group of the inertia field over K with the Galois group of the residue field extension.
informal.NumberField.InertiaGroup_card_eq_ramific: Computes the order of the inertia group as the ramification index of p in L.
informal.Ideal.ramificationIdx_algebra_tower_of_e: Proves multiplicativity of the ramification index in a tower of Dedekind domains.
informal.Ideal.inertiaDeg_algebra_tower_of_eq: Proves multiplicativity of the inertia degree in a tower of Dedekind domains.

records.title: Exact odd-prime distributions of central-binomial valuations
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact distribution of the p-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n) over every complete block 0 <= n < p^k for every odd prime p. The development proves Kummer correctness for padded digit words, constructs the two-state doubling carry enumerator, identifies it with the arithmetic valuation polynomial, derives its second-order recurrence, proves the rational bivariate generating function, and obtains closed formulas for valuations zero and one.

informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.oddPrimeVa: For every odd prime p = 2h+1, proves the denominator-cleared identity for the bivariate series whose coefficient of T^k X^r counts n < p^k with nu_p(binomial(2n,n)) = r; equivalently the series is (1-XT)/(1-(h+1)(1+X)T+pXT^2).
Proves that the exact valuation polynomials satisfy F_{k+2}(X)+pX F_k(X)=(h+1)(1+X)F_{k+1}(X), with F_0=1 and F_1=(h+1)+hX.
informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.padicValNa: Proves Kummer correctness for every valid padded base-p word: the p-adic valuation of its central binomial coefficient equals the number of carries produced by doubling the word.
informal.OddPrimeValuationDistribution.card_oddPr: Gives a closed formula for the number of n below p^(k+2) whose central binomial coefficient has p-adic valuation exactly one.

records.title: Poitou's Explicit Odlyzko Bound for Root Discriminants
records.abstract: Formalizes the unconditional explicit-formula argument for a lower bound on root discriminants of totally complex number fields. Develops the completed Dedekind zeta function and its functional equation, Poitou's explicit formula, the Tartar test function, and a certified numerical estimate proving that degree at least 18 forces root discriminant at least 8.25.

informal.NumberField.Odlyzko.odlyzkoBound: Proves that every totally complex number field of degree at least 18 has absolute discriminant at least 8.25 raised to its degree.

records.title: Classification of groups of order p * q
records.abstract: Classification of noncyclic finite groups of order p*q, including the prime-square direct-product case and the p<q semidirect-product normal form.

informal.OrderPQ.exists_card_eq_prime_mul_prime_a: There exists a noncyclic group of order p*q exactly when p=q, p divides q-1, or q divides p-1.
informal.OrderPQ.nonempty_mulEquiv_of_card_eq_pri: Any two noncyclic groups of order p*q are isomorphic.
informal.OrderPQ.nonempty_mulEquiv_semidirectProd: If p<q, every group of order p*q is isomorphic to a semidirect product of MulZMod q by MulZMod p.

records.title: Osterwalder-Schrader Axioms for the Gaussian Free Field
records.abstract: Formalizes Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for the massive Gaussian free field using Minlos, covariance, and reflection-positivity infrastructure.

informal.OSforGFF.gaussianFreeField_satisfies_all: Proves that the massive Gaussian free field satisfies the OS0-OS4 Osterwalder-Schrader axioms.

records.title: Partial Combinatory Algebras
records.abstract: Formalises partial combinatory algebras with the K/S combinators, programming combinators, the free combinatory algebra, and the graph model.

informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.PCA: Defines the class of partial combinatory algebras (PCAs) with K and S combinators.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.CA: Defines total combinatory algebras and exhibits every total combinatory algebra as a PCA.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.Free: Constructs the free total combinatory algebra as a quotient of formal expressions.
informal.LeanPool.PartialCombinatoryAlgebras.Grap: Constructs the graph-model combinatory algebra on the powerset of any Listing-typed carrier.

records.title: Almost all primes are partially regular
records.abstract: Formalizes an asymptotic theorem about partial regularity of primes via Bernoulli-number irregularity.

informal.LeanPool.PartialRegularity.Extension.irr: Proves the asymptotic big-O bound behind the partial-regularity theorem.

records.title: PCF Theory
records.abstract: Formalizes foundational results from Shelah's Possible Cofinality theory, including the existence of club-guessing sequences.

informal.Ordinal.exists_isClubGuessing_of_cof_unc: Proves the existence of a club-guessing sequence on a stationary set whose elements share a common uncountable cofinality bounded by the cofinality of the ambient ordinal.

records.title: Optimal Pebbling Number of the Hypercube
records.abstract: Formalizes that the optimal pebbling number of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n is Theta((4/3)^n).  Builds a weight-function lower bound of (4/3)^n and a probabilistic recursive upper bound C * (4/3)^n with an explicit constant, combining them into a two-sided big-Theta witness.

informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.optimalPebb: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n has order (4/3)^n: there is a positive constant C with (4/3)^n <= o(Q_n) <= C * (4/3)^n for all n.
informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.lower_bound: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at least (4/3)^n, proved by a weight-function argument summing one-pebble weights over the cube.
informal.PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.upper_bound: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at most C * (4/3)^n for an explicit constant C, via a probabilistic recursive splitting construction.

records.title: Euler's pentagonal number theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a generating-function identity for power series and for real/complex numbers, with a partition-recurrence corollary and a self-contained Franklin-style combinatorial proof.

informal.pentagonalNumberTheorem_powerSeries: Proves Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a formal power series identity ∏(1-xⁿ) = Σ(-1)ᵏ x^(k(3k-1)/2).
informal.pentagonalNumberTheorem_complex: Proves the analytic version of the pentagonal number theorem for real or complex numbers of norm less than one.
informal.Nat.Partition.sum_partition: Derives Euler's pentagonal recurrence for the partition function from the pentagonal number theorem.

records.title: Stable phase retrieval for Hermite-Fock expansions
records.abstract: Formalizes stable phase retrieval for finite Hermite-Fock polynomials and their Gaussian L2 closure in d complex dimensions, together with the quantitative one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate that underlies it.

informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.stable_phase_r: Proves stable phase retrieval for the Gaussian L2 closure of finite d-dimensional Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level, giving a uniform stability constant bounding the phase-aligned L2 distance by the L2 distance of magnitudes.
informal.FockSPR.orthogonalReduction_exists_phase: Proves the phase-aligned one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate, producing a unit phase for which the L2 distance to one is controlled by the magnitude defect.
informal.FockSPR.orthogonalReduction_core: Proves the quantitative centered core estimate bounding the Gaussian Fock norm of a polynomial with small norm by the magnitude defect against one.
informal.FockSPR.LocalFockSPR: Proves the local Fock-space stable phase retrieval coercivity estimate for centered polynomials.
informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.HermitePoly: Defines the normalized one-variable complex Hermite-Fock basis polynomial.
informal.DimdPolyShowcaseChallenge.TrueHermiteFun: Defines the Gaussian L2 closure of finite Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level.

records.title: Accelerated Nesterov convergence under local Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions
records.abstract: Formalizes accelerated Nesterov convergence near a smooth minimizer manifold under a local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, including embedded-manifold and C3 public theorem statements with explicit exponential rate and prefactor.

informal.PLAcceleratedNesterovLean.nesterov_pl_ac: Proves an accelerated Nesterov convergence rate for state positions near a C2 embedded minimizer manifold, with an existential momentum parameter, explicit exponential decay, and prefactor 2.
Proves the corresponding C3 public theorem, deriving the minimizer geometry internally from smoothness and the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
informal.PLAcceleratedNesterovLean.nesterov_conve: Provides the reusable local theta-retuned convergence theorem used by the public accelerated-rate statements.

records.title: Poincaré's Nonintegrability Theorem for the Restricted Three-Body Problem
records.abstract: Formalizes Poincaré's classical parameter-analytic nonintegrability theorem for the planar circular restricted three-body problem. The development defines the rotating-frame Hamiltonian on its collision-free domain, proves logarithmic blow-up of the resonant disturbing average at an apoapsis collision boundary, and analytically propagates the resulting dense resonant obstruction to exclude an additional analytic first integral. The final statement is the fixed-coordinate, global uniform-domain special case of the planar part of Yagasaki's Theorem 1.1; his local meromorphic resonant-orbit obstruction is Theorem 3.1.

informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.nonintegrabil: No jointly real-analytic family near zero mass can be an additional first integral of the planar circular restricted three-body Hamiltonian with phase differential independent from the Hamiltonian differential anywhere on the uniform collision-free domain.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.delaunayHomol: If the first homological equation holds and its perturbing Fourier coefficient is nonzero at every positive rational Kepler resonance, then the leading differential of a putative analytic first integral is nowhere independent of the unperturbed Hamiltonian frequency.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.delaunayDense: For the rotating Kepler frequency in Delaunay actions, orthogonality of a continuous candidate differential to every positive rational resonance vector forces dependence with the Hamiltonian frequency at every positive action.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.homologicalEq: At a resonant action in two degrees of freedom, a nonzero perturbing Fourier mode and the first homological equation force the unperturbed frequency and the differential of a putative leading first-integral coefficient to be linearly dependent.
informal.LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.denseResonanc: If the resonant obstruction holds on a dense set of actions and the frequency and differential vary continuously, then they are linearly dependent at every action.

records.title: Pointwise Birkhoff Ergodic Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the pointwise Birkhoff ergodic theorem for integrable real-valued observables.

informal.LeanPool.PointwiseBirkhoff.birkhoffErgod: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of Birkhoff averages to invariant conditional expectation for any integrable real-valued observable.
Proves the measurable-observable version of the pointwise Birkhoff ergodic theorem.

records.title: Pólya's enumeration theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Pólya's enumeration theorem counting orbits of colorings under a group action.

informal.LeanPool.PolyaEnumerationTheorem.polya_t: Counts distinct colorings of a finite set under a group action by averaging powers of the number of colors over cycle indices.

records.title: Polylean Unit Conjecture Counterexample
records.abstract: Formalizes Gardam's counterexample to Kaplansky's Unit Conjecture, including the Promislow group, group rings, torsion-freeness of the group, and the non-trivial unit in 𝔽₂[P].

informal.LeanPool.Polylean.P.torsionFree: Proves that the Promislow group used in Gardam's construction is torsion-free.
informal.LeanPool.Polylean.Gardam.GardamTheorem: Proves Gardam's counterexample to Kaplansky's Unit Conjecture by constructing a non-trivial unit in the group ring 𝔽₂[P].

records.title: The polynomial method and restricted sums of congruence classes
records.abstract: Formalizes the polynomial method (Alon–Tarsi-style combinatorial Nullstellensatz arguments) and applies it to restricted sums of congruence classes, including Cauchy–Davenport, Dias da Silva–Hamidoune, and a Vandermonde coefficient formula.

informal.ANR_polynomial_method: The Alon–Nathanson–Rusza polynomial method theorem, giving a non-vanishing-coefficient criterion for restricted sums.
informal.cauchy_davenport: The Cauchy–Davenport theorem on sums of subsets of the cyclic group of prime order.
informal.dias_da_silva_hamidoune: The Dias da Silva–Hamidoune lower bound for restricted sums of distinct elements in a prime cyclic group.
informal.restricted_sum_distinct_sizes: A lower bound for restricted sums when the summand sets have distinct sizes.
informal.Vandermonde_coefficient_formula: A closed-form expression for a specific Vandermonde-style coefficient used by the polynomial method.

records.title: Pumping Lemma for Context-Free Grammars
records.abstract: Formalizes the pumping lemma for context-free languages via parse trees of Chomsky-normal-form grammars and a pigeonhole argument.

informal.Language.IsContextFree.pumping: Every context-free language admits a pumping length p such that any word of length at least p decomposes as u v x y z with vy nonempty, vxy of length at most p, and u vⁱ x yⁱ z in the language for every i.
informal.ChomskyNormalFormGrammar.pumping: The pumping lemma at the level of a Chomsky-normal-form grammar, obtained from a sufficiently tall parse tree with a repeated nonterminal.

records.title: Polynomial parametrizations of Pythagorean triples
records.abstract: Formalizes Frisch and Vaserstein's result that Pythagorean triples are not parametrizable by one triple of integer-coefficient polynomials in any number of variables, but are parametrizable by a single triple of integer-valued rational polynomials, including the positive and sixteen-parameter variants.

informal.LeanPool.PythagoreanPolynomialParametriz: Proves that no single triple of integer-coefficient polynomials in any number of variables parametrizes all Pythagorean triples.
Gives the explicit four-variable integer-valued polynomial parametrization of all Pythagorean triples.
Formalizes the positive Pythagorean-triple parametrization with positive parameters and a nonnegative auxiliary parameter.
Converts the positive parametrization to an unrestricted sixteen-integer-parameter parametrization using the four-square theorem.
Proves the cited reduction from one integer-valued polynomial tuple to finitely many integer-coefficient polynomial tuples.
Records the integer-valued polynomial ring non-UFD phenomenon behind the paper's motivating discussion.

records.title: Quasi-Borel Spaces
records.abstract: Formalizes quasi-Borel spaces and quasi-Borel pre-domains, a category for higher-order probability theory.

informal.QuasiBorelSpace: Defines a quasi-Borel space as a type with a set of random variables closed under constants, measurable precomposition, and gluing.
informal.QuasiBorelSpace.IsHom: Defines morphisms of quasi-Borel spaces as maps that preserve random variables under precomposition.
informal.OmegaQuasiBorelSpace: Combines the quasi-Borel and ω-complete partial order structures with the compatibility axiom of Vakar-Kammar-Staton.
informal.QuasiBorelSpace.ProbabilityMeasure: Defines the probability-measure monad on quasi-Borel spaces by quotienting pre-probability measures by integral equivalence.

records.title: The Ramanujan-Nagell theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Ramanujan-Nagell theorem, proving that the Diophantine equation x^2 + 7 = 2^n has exactly the five positive-integer solutions (|x|, n) = (1, 3), (3, 4), (5, 5), (11, 7), (181, 15).

informal.ramanujanNagellExact: Proves that the integer solutions of x^2 + 7 = 2^n are exactly (x, n) = (+/-1, 3), (+/-3, 4), (+/-5, 5), (+/-11, 7), (+/-181, 15).

records.title: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes
records.abstract: Formalizes the ABC-conditional proof that Ramanujan's tau function takes prime values only rarely.

informal.main_theorem: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes.
informal.reduction_lemma: Reduces the main prime-value statement to the key analytic estimates.
informal.abc_bound_E2: ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E2.
informal.abc_bound_E4: ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E4.

records.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Strong n-Conjectures
records.abstract: Formalizes the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture, constructing tuple families whose abc-style quality stays bounded above 1, and proves Browkin-Brzezinski lower bounds on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples.

informal.RamaekersConjecture: Defines Ramaekers's conjecture for fixed n as the statement that the quality of the relevant tuple set equals 1.
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_ge_six: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every n at least 6 (the general case, Theorem 1.14).
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_odd_ge_five: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every odd n at least 5 (the odd case via Pell equations, Theorem 1.13).
informal.not_ramaekersConjecture_five: Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for n equal to 5 (the Konyagin prelude bound).
informal.le_quality_nConjectureTuples: Proves the Browkin-Brzezinski 1994 lower bound 2n-5 on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples (Theorem 1.3).

records.title: Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem: the Sobolev embedding H¹ → L² is a compact operator on compact Riemannian manifolds. The proof builds the Euclidean core (compactness of the H¹ → L² inclusion on a fixed compact support via the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion and the H¹ translation estimate ‖τₐu − u‖₂ ≤ ‖a‖ · ‖∇u‖₂), glues chart contributions over a finite atlas, and specializes to the Levi-Civita Riemannian volume measure.

informal.RellichKondrachov.Geometry.Manifold.Sobo: On a compact Riemannian manifold, the Sobolev inclusion H¹ → L² for the Levi-Civita volume measure is a compact operator.
informal.RellichKondrachov.Analysis.FunctionalSpa: Euclidean Rellich–Kondrachov compactness: on a fixed compact support K, the H¹ → L² inclusion restricted to functions supported in K is a compact operator.
informal.RellichKondrachov.Geometry.Manifold.Sobo: On a compact Riemannian manifold there exists finite chart data equipped with explicit Lipschitz neighborhoods and a subordinate partition of unity, the input to the manifold Rellich glue.

records.title: Riemann Mapping Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes a proof of the Riemann mapping theorem for proper simply connected plane domains with primitives.

informal.RMT: Proves the Riemann mapping theorem for the project's domain hypotheses.
informal.main: Constructs a conformal map from a good domain onto the unit disk.
informal.montel: Proves a Montel compactness theorem for uniformly bounded holomorphic families.
informal.hurwitz: Proves the Hurwitz theorem used to preserve injectivity under limits.

records.title: RL Theory in Lean
records.abstract: Develops probability, Markov-chain, and stochastic-matrix infrastructure for reinforcement-learning theory.

informal.StochasticMatrix.stationary_distribution: Proves existence of a stationary distribution for a stochastic matrix.

records.title: Explicit type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings
records.abstract: Constructs the type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings explicitly over ℤ — from signed intervals on Fin n and from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product — proves the pairing and reflection identities exhibiting them as Mathlib `RootPairing`s, and identifies the BCₙ roots with the classical set {±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, ±eᵢ ± eⱼ}.

informal.An.rootPairing: Constructs the type Aₙ root pairing over the integers from signed intervals on Fin n, with finiteness, reducedness, and crystallographic properties.
informal.BCn.rootPairing: Constructs the type BCₙ root pairing from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ via a symmetric nondegenerate form.
informal.BCn.isReflective_iff_isClassicalRoot: Characterizes the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ as exactly the classical type BCₙ roots ±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, and ±eᵢ ± eⱼ for i ≠ j.
informal.BCn.range_rootPairing_root: Identifies the root set of the type BCₙ root pairing with the classical type BCₙ root set.

records.title: Certified Runge-Kutta Order Conditions
records.abstract: Certifies Runge-Kutta order conditions over planar rooted trees, including RK4 order four, Dormand-Prince order five, and Gauss-Legendre order six.

informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.satisf: Reduces order-p Runge-Kutta conditions to a finite catalogue check over rooted trees.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_or: Certifies that classical RK4 satisfies all planar rooted-tree order conditions through order four.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_no: Shows that RK4 fails a fifth-order condition, pinning its order exactly.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.orderC: Proves order conditions are invariant under permutations of a node's children.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.dp_ord: Certifies the Dormand-Prince RK45 fifth-order tableau through order five.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.gauss_: Certifies the Gauss-Legendre three-stage tableau through order four over Q(sqrt(15)).
Certifies the denominator-cleared (360-scaled) integer Z(sqrt(15)) Gauss-Legendre tableau through order six, the scaled certificate feeding the homogeneity bridge.
Certifies the Gauss-Legendre s=3 tableau through order six over Q(sqrt(15)), via the formalized homogeneity bridge from the 360-scaled integer certificate.

records.title: The Rupert Problem for convex polyhedra
records.abstract: Formalizes the Rupert property for the cube, the regular tetrahedron, and the triakis tetrahedron, exhibiting for each an explicit straight-through hole admitting a congruent copy.

informal.Cube.rupert: Proves that the cube has the Rupert property.
informal.Tetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the regular tetrahedron has the Rupert property.
informal.TriakisTetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the triakis tetrahedron has the Rupert property.

records.title: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
records.abstract: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.

informal.Sabidussi.LoopMultigraph.loop_sabidussi_: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.
The same compatibility statement phrased with the intrinsic even-edge-set circuit decomposition, from which the ordinary-circuit form is derived.

records.title: Moreira's version of Sard's theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Moreira's strengthening of Sard's theorem, bounding the Hausdorff dimension of critical-value images of C^{k+alpha} maps.

informal.hausdorffMeasure_sardMoreiraBound_image_: Proves Hausdorff-measure nullity for images of points where the derivative rank is bounded by p, at Moreira's Sard bound.
informal.dimH_image_le_sardMoreiraBound_of_finran: Converts the measure-null theorem into the headline Hausdorff-dimension upper bound for critical-value images.

records.title: Selberg Sieve
records.abstract: Formalizes the Selberg sieve with applications to prime-counting bounds and a Brun-Titchmarsh-style estimate.

informal.fundamental_theorem_simple: Proves the simple Selberg sieve upper-bound theorem.
informal.primeCounting_isBigO_atTop: Derives the asymptotic prime-counting upper bound.
informal.primeCounting_le_mul: Gives an eventual explicit constant upper bound for the prime-counting function.
informal.primesBetween_le: Bounds the number of primes in an interval using the sieve estimate.

records.title: Genus-Zero Pairings and Catalan Numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite combinatorics behind the genus-zero term of the Wigner semicircle law: a pairing of Fin (2n), viewed as a fixed-point-free involution, has genus zero (total cycle count of the rotation product maximal) exactly when it is noncrossing, and these genus-zero pairings are counted by the Catalan number Cₙ. The Catalan recurrence is obtained from an explicit equivalence decomposing a noncrossing pairing by the partner of vertex 0 into independent inside and outside pairings.

informal.card_noncrossingPairing_eq_catalan: The number of noncrossing pairings on 2n points equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_count: The number of genus-zero pairings of Fin (2n) equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_iff_noncrossing: A pairing has genus zero if and only if it is noncrossing.

records.title: Wigner Semicircle Distribution
records.abstract: Defines the real Wigner semicircle distribution, its normalized density, affine transformations, and finite-moment integrability.

informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDFReal: Defines the real-valued density of the semicircle distribution with mean μ and variance v.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDF: Defines the ℝ≥0∞-valued density of the semicircle distribution.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.integral_semicirc: Proves that the real-valued semicircle density integrates to one for nonzero variance.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal: Defines the semicircle measure on ℝ, equal to a Dirac mass when the variance is zero.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal_ma: Shows that translating a semicircle measure translates its mean parameter.
Shows that scaling by a nonzero constant scales the mean and variance parameters.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.memLp_id_semicirc: Shows that the identity has all finite Lp moments under a semicircle distribution.

records.abstract: Formalizes the quantitative Nisan-Szegedy/Huang sensitivity theorem for Boolean functions.

records.title: The Kunen inconsistency theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes elementary embeddings of models of ZF set theory and proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that there is no nontrivial elementary embedding of the set-theoretic universe into itself.

informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_V: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that every elementary embedding of the von Neumann universe V into itself is the identity.
informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_vonNeumann: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem for von Neumann levels V_μ at a successor-limit ordinal, computing the supremum of the critical-point iterates.
informal.SetTheory.crit: Defines the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding as the least ordinal it moves.
informal.NontrivialElementaryEmbedding: Defines a nontrivial elementary embedding of a model of ZF into itself.

records.title: Shannon Entropy Characterization
records.abstract: Formalizes Shannon's finite-alphabet characterization theorem for entropy from the 1948 paper.

informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves that any finite-alphabet uncertainty functional satisfying Shannon's conditions equals natural-log entropy up to a positive scale.
Restates the characterization for any logarithm base greater than one.
Proves the converse, showing that Shannon entropy satisfies the formal condition bundle.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.chain_: Proves the finite joint-entropy chain rule.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves subadditivity of finite joint entropy.

records.title: Quadratic-order prime classification
records.abstract: Formalizes foundational algebra for quadratic orders associated to discriminants, including their power basis, norm and discriminant identities, odd-prime splitting/ramification/inertness criteria via Legendre symbols, and root-counting results for quadratic congruences modulo odd prime powers.

informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_inert_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is maximal in the quadratic order O_d exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is -1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_ramified_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is not radical in O_d exactly when p divides d.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_split_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is radical but not maximal exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is 1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_copri: Counts roots of x^2 = c modulo p^n for odd prime p and p not dividing c, giving two roots when the Legendre symbol is 1 and none otherwise.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_even_: Counts roots of x^2 = p^(2r) u modulo p^n for odd prime p, p not dividing u, and 2r < n, reducing to the coprime case and multiplying by p^r.
informal.QuadraticOrder.tau_sub_tauConj_sq_of_val: Proves the discriminant identity (tau - tauConj)^2 = d for valid quadratic-order discriminants d congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4.

records.title: Special Numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the Eulerian numbers, Euclid numbers, and Sylvester's sequence from Chapter 6 of Concrete Mathematics, proving Worpitzky's identity for the first and coprimality, monotonicity, and explicit doubly-exponential closed forms for the latter two.

informal.SpecialNumbers.sylvester: Defines Sylvester's sequence by the recurrence e(n+1) = e(n) * (e(n) - 1) + 1.
informal.SpecialNumbers.sylvester_coprime: Shows distinct terms of Sylvester's sequence are coprime.
informal.SpecialNumbers.sylvester_eq_floor_consta: Gives the explicit closed form for Sylvester's sequence as a floor of a doubly-exponential power of a constant.
informal.SpecialNumbers.Euclid.euclid_coprime: Shows distinct Euclid numbers are coprime.
informal.SpecialNumbers.Euclid.euclid_eq_floor_co: Gives the explicit closed form for the Euclid numbers as a floor of a doubly-exponential power of a constant.
informal.SpecialNumbers.eulerian: Defines the Eulerian numbers via their standard triangular recurrence and boundary values.
informal.SpecialNumbers.worpitzky: Proves Worpitzky's identity, expanding the power x^n in the binomial-coefficient basis with Eulerian-number coefficients.

records.title: Spectral positivity
records.abstract: Perron-Frobenius theory, Jentzsch's theorem, and matrix/operator positivity in Lean 4. At the matrix level it proves that nonnegative matrices have nonnegative powers, the Metzler decomposition and positivity of the matrix exponential of a Metzler matrix, M-matrix inverse positivity, and the Perron-Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices (a positive dominant eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector). At the operator level it proves Jentzsch's theorem for compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operators on L2 — a simple, strictly positive ground state with a spectral gap — together with a kernel positivity criterion.

informal.allpos_has_pos_eigenvec: A matrix with all strictly positive entries has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector (Perron-Frobenius for positive matrices, via the Collatz-Wielandt characterization).
informal.perron_frobenius: An irreducible (primitive) nonnegative matrix has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector.
informal.ground_state_strictly_positive: The ground eigenfunction of a compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operator on L2 is strictly positive almost everywhere (Jentzsch).
informal.SpectralPositivity.Matrix.MMatrix.invers: The inverse of a nonsingular irreducible M-matrix is entrywise strictly positive.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: teorth/sendov
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Sendov's conjecture, and of its Phelps-Rodriguez strengthening, in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial p of degree n >= 2 lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero a of p has a critical point of p within distance 1 of it, and within distance strictly less than 1 unless |a| = 1 and p is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n. The proof is by contradiction. Degrees 2 to 4 fall to an elementary integral computation; degree 5 upward goes through two estimates on the same integral -- a polar channel and an origin channel -- which are shown to be incompatible, reducing the theorem to a single numerical inequality. That inequality is discharged by exact rational Bernstein certificates, generated outside Lean and re-verified inside it, in both of its ranges: per-degree certificates for 5 <= n <= 100, and, for n >= 101, a single degree-58 certificate closing the one-variable inequality that the analytic large-degree reduction leaves behind. The boundary case |a| = 1 is proved separately from a reciprocal identity, and it is there that the equality classification is extracted. Nothing here is claimed to be new: the informal proof being formalized is a digestion of Lech Mazur's proof, which had already been formalized in Lean, so this is a second and independently checkable machine-checked proof of Sendov's conjecture, whose additional content is the Phelps-Rodriguez equality case. The Lean source was written by an AI agent under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the two deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and no floating point in any statement or proof.

records.title: AxiomMath/PrimeGapsLib
records.abstract: `PrimeGapsLib` is an evolving codebase aimed at housing results about gaps in primes. The flagship result thus far is that pairs of primes are separated by at most 246 infinitely often, conditional on the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem. The 246 proof was generated collaboratively between human formalisers at Axiom Math and AxiomProver, their in-house theorem proving system. Community feedback and contributions are welcome!

records.title: xinjiegit/ben_27_formalization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that there are absolute constants c > 0 and p₀ such that, for every prime p ≥ p₀, the minimum size m(p) of a set A ⊆ 𝔽_p with |A| ≥ 2 and no uniquely represented sum satisfies m(p) ≥ c (log p / log log p)².  Here representations are unordered two-element multisets from A, repeated summands are allowed, and "no unique sum" means that every such multiset has a distinct equal-sum mate.

records.title: rkirov/jordan_pick
records.abstract: The Jordan curve theorem, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib: a continuous injective map from the circle into the plane has a complement with exactly two connected components. The hypothesis is bare continuity and injectivity — no smoothness, piecewise-linearity or rectifiability — which is what makes the theorem hard and what separates it from the polygonal case. The proof follows Maehara's reduction to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, via a crossing lemma for transversal paths in a rectangle and the fact that every component has the curve as its boundary, together with a farthest-pair normalization that pins down exactly one bounded component. Because Mathlib has no Brouwer fixed point theorem at the pinned revision, Brouwer is built here from the ground up: covering-space path lifting for the circle giving π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, then no-retraction of the disk onto its boundary, then Brouwer on the disk by ray-retraction, then the general nonempty-compact-convex case by nearest-point projection. The statement is expressed in Mathlib's own vocabulary. The proof is sorry-free and depends on Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and nothing else.

records.title: elliotglazer/erdos501
records.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.title: WillWhistler/Regts-Sevenster
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, proved in both directions and resting on no assumption. A complex-valued graph parameter that is normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is the partition function of a mixed edge-colouring model; and when the rank base is R the model may be taken with k even and ℓ odd colours satisfying k, 2ℓ ≤ ⌊2eR⌋. Nothing is assumed. Deligne's theorem on tensor categories, on which the forward direction rests, is itself proved in the development — in the fibre-functor form that is the substance of Deligne's own proof, and by a route through simple algebras in the ind-completion rather than his descent argument — and each of its hypotheses is discharged for a concretely constructed rigid symmetric monoidal envelope of the parameter's skein category. The symmetric-group character theory the argument needs is proved from Mathlib's linear algebra rather than cited, and the converse direction reproves Regts and Sevenster's own theorem. Every theorem of record depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, pinned in-tree so that a change to the axiom set is a build failure rather than a review task.

records.title: vo-rodrigues/wallace-problem-palomar
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology in which every convergent sequence is eventually constant, and constructs a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative topological monoid that is not a group, giving a negative answer to Wallace's question.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem A (ODE rigidity, all weights; label thm:ode, Theorem 6.1 in the current compilation of the campaign paper): if polynomials A, C over an integral domain of characteristic zero and an integer weight nu >= 1 satisfy A*C' - nu*A'*C = c for a nonzero constant c, then deg A <= 1 (TheoremA).  Also a standalone positive-characteristic strengthening extracted from the same proof (TheoremA_charP): the same conclusion over a domain of characteristic p under the degree bounds nu*deg A < p and deg C < p.  The theorem is the rigidity engine of the depth-two block analysis in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

records.title: stalex444/arithmetic-of-time
records.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate.

records.title: stalex444/pdt-lean
records.abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the vertex-gap obstruction at (k,d2) = (2,2) (label thm:22, Theorem 3.4 in the current compilation) from the campaign paper "A Vertex-Gap Obstruction for Low-Degree Strip Pairs in the Plane Jacobian Conjecture": for polynomials P, Q in K[x,y] over a field K of characteristic not in {2,3,5}, supported in the normalized type-(2,2) Newton strips along (1,2) with [P,Q] = x^2, the block coefficients satisfy a3 = 0 and a2^2*a6 = 0 - so the generic chart a2*a6 != 0 of the strip family is empty (VertexGap22, plus the side-symmetric companion VertexGap22_swapped in the mirrored labels). Also formalized: the arithmetic corner-enumeration lemma behind the vertex normalization (lem:enum, Lemma 2.2; CornerEnumeration) and the side-symmetric form of the gap condition, hypothesis (ii) as corrected by the erratum recorded in Section 8 (GapConditionSideSymm).  The theorem is the mechanism that empties the generic chart of the (8,28) strip subcase in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

records.title: yuanchenyang/lean_low_rank_univariate_sos
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.

records.title: catskillsresearch/cardb
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of an exact enumeration identity and two consequences: for a finite type α, the number of families B ⊆ Set α that are topological bases equals the sum, over all topologies τ on α, of 2^(|τ| − |M_τ|), where M_τ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighbourhoods (Mathlib's nhdsKer {x} at each point). Kernel-reducible enumeration gives the exact table #(0)=2, #(1)=2, #(2)=10, #(3)=142. A quantitative sandwich then shows that the discrete fiber 2^(2^N − N) dominates: for N ≥ 2 the remaining fibers contribute at most 2^(N(N−1) + 3·2^(N−2)), the ratio to the discrete term tends to 1, and for N ≥ 10 the total is at most twice the discrete term. The argument is a fiber decomposition: every finite topology is Alexandrov-discrete, the minimal neighbourhoods generate it, and the bases generating τ are exactly the families B with M_τ ⊆ B ⊆ {U | τ.IsOpen U}. The informal account is the companion note CARDB.md in this repository. The Lean source was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.
